package.name: openaid-se
package.author: Swedish MFA
package.notes:
Open dataset for Swedish development assistance from the 1970s to present times. Providing information on finance, statstics and public records shown from aggegated levels to specific aid activities. This data is included into the dataset:iati-registry but is also available via an API on Openaid.se. 

The data comes from a variety of sources, mainly from Sida - the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency - and the Swedish Ministry for Foreign Affairs. package.name: fts
package.author: Sean Foo
package.notes:
The FTS is a global, real-time database which records all reported global international humanitarian aid.
## Details
The FTS is a global, real-time database which records all reported international hummanitarian aid (including that for NGOs and the Red Cross / Red Crescent Movement, bilateral aid, in-kind aid, and private donations). FTS features a special focus on consolidated and flash appeals, because they cover the major humanitarian crises and because their funding requirements are well defined - which allows FTS to indicate to what extent populations in crisis receive humanitarian aid in proportion to needs. FTS is managed by the UN Office for Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA). All FTS data are provided by donors or recipient organisations.
The FTS is a web-based searchable database of humanitarian requirements and contributions.  It serves to analyse aid and monitor accountability among humanitarian actors, by clearly indicating to what extent a certain population receives humanitarian relief aid, and in what proportion to needs.  The FTS offers a series of standard tables that show humanitarian aid flows in various formats, and also allows users to produce custom financial tables on demand.
package.title: Financial Tracking Service (FTS)

package.name: dise-o-web-lo-hago-yo-o-contrato
package.notes:
En la actualidad, casi el 90% de las empresas españolas  tienen presencia en internet, ya sea a través de su página corporativa o a través de tiendas online.

El problema es que para desarrollar su sitio web, a menudo recurren a empresas poco profesionales o de dudosa reputación con tal de ahorrarse un dinero.
Si uno navega por la red, podrá observar que en este sector lo barato acaba saliendo caro. Son innumerables las empresas que ponen en manos de gente poco preparada su proyecto y acaban en el “pozo” en los resultados de los buscadores.

Cuando se quiere desarrollar un diseño web para una empresa es muy importante tener en cuenta los siguientes factores:

Que el desarrollador tenga una buena formación y experiencia. De este modo evitaremos las auténticas chapuzas que estamos acostumbrados a ver a diario.
Que haya una implicación mutua en el proyecto. Así conseguiremos que el sitio web transmita la imagen de la empresa.

Que haya un buen estudio sobre la competencia para recoger en nuestro proyecto lo mejor de ésta y mejorar sus puntos débiles.

Que haya una continua actualización de contenido ya que hoy en día los buscadores prefieren los sitios dinámicos a los estáticos.

Que haya una campaña SEO continua para que podamos escalar posiciones de búsqueda.

Muchas son las empresas que, a pesar de esto y a riesgo de conseguir un resultado mediocre, prefieren desarrollar por si mismas su proyecto.

Por ello, y con el fin de mejorar los contenidos de la red, desde este blog haremos recomendaciones para optimizar nuestros sitios web.

Un saludo

José María Somoza
CEO de PYME Networks, [Diseño web en Madrid] (http://www.pymenetworks.es)
package.title: Diseño web ¿Lo hago yo o contrato?

package.name: fts
package.title: Financial Tracking Service (FTS)
package.notes:
The FTS is a global, real-time database which records all reported global international humanitarian aid.
## Details
The FTS is a global, real-time database which records all reported international hummanitarian aid (including that for NGOs and the Red Cross / Red Crescent Movement, bilateral aid, in-kind aid, and private donations). FTS features a special focus on consolidated and flash appeals, because they cover the major humanitarian crises and because their funding requirements are well defined - which allows FTS to indicate to what extent populations in crisis receive humanitarian aid in proportion to needs. FTS is managed by the UN Office for Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA). All FTS data are provided by donors or recipient organisations.
The FTS is a web-based searchable database of humanitarian requirements and contributions.  It serves to analyse aid and monitor accountability among humanitarian actors, by clearly indicating to what extent a certain population receives humanitarian relief aid, and in what proportion to needs.  The FTS offers a series of standard tables that show humanitarian aid flows in various formats, and also allows users to produce custom financial tables on demand.
package.author: Sean Foo
